questions.question: 1. Which of the following is the most basic searching algorithm?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Binary search is more efficient but requires sorted data.
explanations.b: Correct. Linear search checks each element one by one.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Jump search is less basic than linear search.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Interpolation search is more advanced.

questions.question: 2. Which sorting algorithm repeatedly swaps adjacent elements if they are in the wrong order?

explanations.a: Correct. Bubble sort swaps adjacent elements.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Selection sort selects the minimum element.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Insertion sort builds the sorted list one element at a time.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Merge sort divides and merges arrays.

questions.question: 3. What is the time complexity of binary search in a sorted array?

explanations.a: Incorrect. O(n) is for linear search.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(n^2) is for some sorting algorithms.
explanations.c: Correct. Binary search divides the array in half each time.
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(1) is for constant time operations.

questions.question: 4. Which of the following is NOT a comparison-based sorting algorithm?

explanations.b: Correct. Counting sort uses counting, not comparisons.

questions.question: 5. Which searching algorithm is best suited for finding an element in a sorted array?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Linear search is less efficient for sorted arrays.
explanations.b: Correct. Binary search is optimal for sorted arrays.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Jump search is less common.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Exponential search is for unbounded arrays.

questions.question: 6. Which sorting algorithm has the best average-case time complexity?

explanations.c: Correct. Merge sort is O(n log n) on average.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Insertion sort is slower for large data.

questions.question: 7. Which of the following statements about searching and sorting is TRUE?

answers.a: Binary search works on unsorted data.
answers.b: Bubble sort is faster than merge sort for large data.
answers.d: Linear search is always faster than binary search.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Binary search requires sorted data.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Merge sort is faster for large data.
explanations.c: Correct. Sorting allows faster searching algorithms.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Binary search is faster for sorted data.
